issues.legal_issue: An agreement to sell leased premises does not by itself terminate the tenancy; termination depends on whether the parties intended to surrender the lease.
material_facts: The tenant entered into an agreement to purchase the leased premises from the landlord while the tenancy was subsisting and asserted that he had paid part of the consideration.
The agreement contained no term addressing the fate of the tenancy or expressly providing for surrender.
The tenant remained in possession, and the landlord sought eviction under the applicable rent law after determining the tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The agreement did not determine the tenancy or end the landlord-tenant relationship. The landlord was entitled to seek eviction after determining the tenancy, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 111(e) and (f) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a lease may be determined by express surrender or implied surrender. Applying Shah Mathuradas Maganlal & Co. v. Nagappa Shankarappa Malage & Ors. (1976) 3 SCC 660, surrender requires mutual yielding of the lease or circumstances showing implied surrender, such as creation of a new relationship or relinquishment of possession. The agreement must be assessed for the parties’ intention. R. Kanthimathi v. Beatrice Xavier (Mrs.) (2000) 9 SCC 339 was distinguishable because the agreement there expressly referred to the premises having been surrendered into the purchaser’s possession. The landlord’s application was maintainable under Section 21(1)(a) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, once the tenancy had been determined.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_appeal and sale_agreement_during_tenancy and agreement_contains_no_surrender_term and no_surrender_by_conduct

predicates.tenant_eviction_appeal: The matter came before the court as an appeal in a landlord’s rent-law eviction proceeding.
predicates.sale_agreement_during_tenancy: The landlord and tenant entered into an agreement to sell the leased premises while the tenancy was subsisting.
predicates.agreement_contains_no_surrender_term: The sale agreement contained no term stating that the tenancy would end or be surrendered.
predicates.no_surrender_by_conduct: The parties’ conduct did not show that the tenant relinquished possession or that the landlord took possession in a manner amounting to surrender.

issues.definition: When an appeal in an eviction proceeding concerns a sale agreement made during the tenancy, and neither the agreement nor the parties’ conduct shows surrender, the agreement does not terminate the tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: A finding that a landlord has a bona fide need for the premises is not disturbed on appeal when it is a factual finding and is not perverse.
material_facts: The landlord had retired and asserted that he had no other suitable house of his own in the city for himself and his family.
The High Court found that the landlord had established a bona fide need for residence.
The Supreme Court found no perversity or other good ground to interfere with the High Court’s factual finding.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s finding of bona fide need was upheld and was not disturbed on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Bona fide need under Section 21(1)(a) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 was treated as a question of fact. The Supreme Court held that the High Court’s factual finding did not call for interference because it was not perverse.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_appeal and landlord_needs_premises_for_self_or_family and landlord_lacks_other_suitable_home and lower_court_finding_not_perverse

predicates.tenant_eviction_appeal: The matter came before the court as an appeal concerning an eviction proceeding.
predicates.landlord_needs_premises_for_self_or_fami: The landlord asserted that the premises were needed for the landlord’s own residence or the residence of family members.
predicates.landlord_lacks_other_suitable_home: The landlord had no other suitable home available for that residential need.
predicates.lower_court_finding_not_perverse: The appellate court’s finding on the landlord’s need was not shown to be perverse.

issues.definition: In an eviction appeal, when the landlord needs the premises for the landlord or family, has no other suitable home, and the lower court’s finding is not perverse, that finding remains upheld.
